observations.text: Selection, mechanical: commit b441715 touches tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs (the S2 oracle), tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs (S1) and tests/acceptance/support/review_app/app.rs (the shared support). Test-impact tooling gave no answer: argv 'code-fact impacted-tests tests/acceptance/support/review_app/app.rs tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs --root .' exit 124 after a 100 s timeout, empty stdout, empty stderr; an earlier unbounded run also returned nothing within 120 s. Fallback selection used, degraded loud: the slice's own declared verification command over the changed oracle. The selection is incomplete for any other suite that compiles the shared support module; S1's reviewer covers that suite.

The revision is additive only: 'git show b441715 --numstat' reports 18 added and 0 deleted lines in tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs and 129 added and 0 deleted lines in tests/acceptance/support/review_app/app.rs; 'git show b441715 -- <oracle> | grep -c ^-[^-]' returns 0. Every approved assertion, WHAT/WHY/HOW failure message and Gherkin docstring of the three scenarios is preserved byte for byte.

Measured run on this Mac host: argv 'cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_legacy_run_repos_read -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture', exit 0, stdout 'test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 6.02s', 10.33 s wall including the cargo build, no stderr diagnostics. Production for P2 is already landed (crates/review-domain/src/views/queue.rs:652 gates the line on an Option), so this run is GREEN and the semantic RED recorded at the first approval is retained rather than re-observed.

The printed evidence agrees with the assertions in all three scenarios. Legacy run: stored status 'completed', status region one line 'Ownership re-checked - 10 new suggestions', then 'the repos-read line: ABSENT, her queue saying neither repos read nor repo read anywhere' (E4). Five planned repos read: '5 repos read' PRESENT (E5). One planned repo read none: '0 repos read' PRESENT beside 'Skipped priyaraman/kelp: archived since you chose it.' (E5, and the nought-is-still-a-count distinction).

Semantic-RED integrity: show_queue_evidence is the trailing statement of each of the three scenarios, after every then_ step; it asserts nothing and its returned value is discarded. A failing assertion panics before it runs, so it can neither mask a semantic failure nor substitute a new one. It introduces no skip, no expected-fail, no conditional path and no production stub.

Template rule 'No examiner-specific runner, value selector or verbose support mode': satisfied. The printing is unconditional in every run of the suite - plain println!, no cfg attribute, no environment variable, no verbosity flag, no mode parameter, no new runner and no selection of which values to emit. It becomes visible through libtest's own standard --nocapture, which the already-declared EXAMINE entry point scripts/examine/review-app-oracle forwards as an ordinary libtest argument.

No silent-wrong in the printed claim: the ABSENT/PRESENT verdict is computed over the visible text of GET /review, exactly the population the scenario's own assertion searches (support scan_summary at tests/acceptance/support/review_app/repos_and_accounts.rs:1130 is browser.open(/review).text()), and a repos-read wording found outside the role=status region prints a distinct third wording instead of a confident ABSENT. Honest limitation: the helper issues a second GET, so it is a fresh observation of the same page rather than the asserted bytes; it is evidence only and can never create a false green.

typesafe: unavailable. argv 'python3 /Users/jeffbailey/.claude/skills/nw-typesafe-system-one/scripts/jev_decide.py --request - --output -' with three reviewer-owned questions on stdin (template-rule classification, weakened-observation, misleading-evidence), exit 3, stdout 'typesafe: unavailable (TYPESAFE_API_KEY is absent from this process environment...)'; the key is absent from the login shell too. Those three judgments were made locally from the diff, the support source and the measured run.

Obligation closure for P2 is unchanged and total. E4 is falsified by a_run_kept_before_scan_plans_were_stored_says_nothing_about_repos_read over both wordings and the whole page; E5 by a_scan_that_read_the_repos_it_planned_says_how_many and by a_scan_that_could_read_none_of_the_repos_it_planned_still_says_so, the counterexample that rejects hiding the line whenever the count is nought. Every other observation in the file is a scenario-validity guard against a vacuous pass (finished-scan queue, kept suggestions, the named unreadable repo), not an extra promise.

Scope note, not a defect: S2 declares only crates/openlore-review-app/Cargo.toml as a support, while the new helper lives in tests/acceptance/support/review_app/app.rs, declared as a support of S1. The S2 oracle already compiled and used that whole support module before this commit (mod review_app, Browser, rra_world_on_v1_store), so this is no new dependency class, the file was edited by its declared owner inside this same feature, and no promise or observation of S2 depends on the declaration's wording. Recorded for truth, raised as no finding.

Retained from the first approval, outside this delta: the three scenarios are real-IO acceptance scenarios that start the real review-app binary, so each is far above the 10 ms default per-test budget, and the suite also runs two support self-tests (review_app::state_delta::tests). This commit adds only six local HTTP GETs across the suite; measured suite time 6.02 s, well under the 300 s default CI ceiling. No new timing judgment is opened.

diagnostic: ACCEPTED, no findings. The S2 oracle at commit b441715 keeps every approved assertion and its semantic RED intact, and the printing is allowed under the template rule. Evidence: the diff is additive only (18 added, 0 deleted lines in tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs; 129 added, 0 deleted in the shared support), so every then_ step, failure message and Gherkin docstring is byte-identical to the approved oracle; the one added call per scenario is the trailing statement after every assertion, asserts nothing and discards its value, so it can neither mask a semantic failure nor stand in for one. The rule is satisfied because the output is unconditional in every run - no runner, environment variable, cfg gate, verbosity flag, mode parameter or value selector - and is surfaced only by libtest's own --nocapture, which the declared EXAMINE entry point already forwards. Measured on this Mac host: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_legacy_run_repos_read -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture, exit 0, 5 passed in 6.02s, and the printed evidence matches the assertions (legacy run: repos-read line ABSENT, for E4; five planned repos: '5 repos read' PRESENT; one planned repo read none: '0 repos read' PRESENT, for E5). P2 production is already landed, so this run is GREEN and the earlier semantic RED is retained, not restamped. The ABSENT/PRESENT claim reads the same GET /review text the assertion searches and prints a distinct third wording when the wording sits outside the status region, so it cannot report a confident falsehood. Limits held open: test-impact tooling returned no answer (code-fact impacted-tests, exit 124, empty output), so selection fell back to the slice's declared verification command and covers no other suite compiling the shared support; Jev was unavailable (exit 3, no TYPESAFE_API_KEY), so the three semantic judgments are local. Non-blocking notes, no remediation owed: the helper's second GET is a fresh observation of the same page rather than the asserted bytes, and app.rs is declared as an S1 support though the S2 oracle already compiled it.
